answer: A shared staking vault makes each identity expensive: to join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet, one verified attestation at a time and rate-limited per epoch, instead of flooding in at once. Honest work then flows like a river, with rewards paid only after peers attest the output, so a Sybil flood earns nothing without real, costly, verified work.
